items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: And we did that one with the same cast except Elvin Jones played the drums and I added Hubert Laws

ctx.x: Oh yeah. And I’m very proud of that record. And then we made a sequel in 1968. By then Milestone is up and running and she made a deal with Japanese Victor, they owned the tape — no she owns the tape but they had the rights for America, or some kind of complicated deal. And we did that one with the same cast except Elvin Jones played the drums and I added Hubert Laws and I also made those charts. Then we made a third record in 1980 was it or ’79 for another label called — a now defunct label called Inner City but…
them reissued here. It seems to be not easy. But we’re hoping, soon. Those records I’ll stand on.

items.q: I didn’t know I played with him. I don’t remember playing the record with him.

ctx.x: I kind of remember that too.
